evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the user need (creating a game) with minimal input details; does not prescribe UI widgets/technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to invite via a link; does not dictate UI components or implementation mechanisms beyond the concept of a URL.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (single multi-line text field) rather than just the need to enter an item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (visibility of items) without prescribing a specific UI/technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the capability needed (choose an item) without specifying UI controls or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the functional need (add item) without prescribing how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to edit items; no concrete UI/technical mechanism is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to remove an item; does not prescribe solution details.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior (reveal estimates early) without specifying UI widgets or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Defines a business rule/need (use average) rather than prescribing technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element/behavior (“estimate” field auto-filled) instead of only stating the need (speed up accepting unanimous estimates).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the need to record the agreed estimate; does not mandate a particular UI control or technical approach.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need for re-estimation; no solution details are imposed.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need (bulk import) without prescribing file formats/technical mechanisms beyond the general concept of a spreadsheet.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: States a user workflow need (copy/paste from spreadsheet) without specifying UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find prior games; does not prescribe a specific UI/technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (see transcript) without prescribing export formats or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete storage/export format (HTML file), which is a solution choice rather than just the need to export/save a transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export/storage format (CSV), which is an implementation/solution decision.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove a game and its data; does not prescribe technical deletion mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Describes required information for account creation; does not mandate specific UI widgets or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: States the authentication need; does not prescribe UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to update account info without prescribing how it is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove an account and associated data; no solution details are mandated.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need (localized time display) without prescribing implementation.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism/channel (by email) rather than stating the need to recover access after forgetting a password.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a stakeholder need to choose between two estimation scales; this is domain behavior rather than an implementation/UI prescription.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a capacity requirement (team size) without prescribing technical solution details.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to join and identify oneself; minor UI mention (“page”) is not a concrete widget/implementation prescription.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States an information need without prescribing how it is displayed.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses visibility need; no solution details are mandated.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: States a feedback/awareness need without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior (simultaneous reveal) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: States a rule about when changes are allowed; does not prescribe technical/UI implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need (history visibility) without prescribing UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States an information need; no solution details are mandated.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific solution mechanism and parameter (“two-minute countdown timer”) rather than the underlying need to timebox discussion.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Builds on a specific solution artifact (“two-minute timer”) and dictates its automatic reset behavior, which is implementation/solution-oriented.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to review prior information; “scroll back” is a UI interaction but not a concrete widget/technical mechanism prescription.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency need in the domain interaction; does not prescribe implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: States a rule/need about estimate changes without prescribing solution details.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes concrete UI presentation details (small thumbnail photo, placement) rather than the need (make the game more personal).

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical standards/implementation choices (XHTML/CSS compliance) rather than stating the underlying accessibility/compatibility need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a documentation/communication need without prescribing technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Directly prescribes a technical mechanism (database indexes) instead of the need (fast queries/performance).

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical targets (named browser versions), which are solution constraints rather than a pure stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific standard (W3C accessibility guidelines) as the solution approach rather than stating the accessibility need in problem terms.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a performance need without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a capability/need (support many languages/characters); while “Unicode” is a technical term, it expresses the required capability rather than an internal implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: States a user-facing need about URL structure without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user experience need; does not prescribe specific UI widgets or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a privacy/anonymization need without prescribing specific storage formats or algorithms.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (usage metrics) without prescribing how metrics are collected or displayed.
